thread:
sara-finance: FYI customer AcmeCorp reported a failed partial refund after a mid-cycle downgrade — PO required and tax-exempt flag involved. Invoice INV-2026-0421 shows only a partial credit applied, remainder still on the card. :confused:

mike-support: Which invoice line(s) are we talking about? they upgraded then downgraded in the same billing period?

sara-finance: They were on Pro yearly, downgraded to Standard mid-cycle on 2026-03-09. Billing system created proration but because the PO requires tax-exempt status the tax calculation path went through the legacy tax engine. Result: credit split into two credit notes, one with tax lines and one without — Stripe only refunded one CN and left a balance.

alex-billing: Can you paste invoice and credit note IDs? I want to check ledger entries and Stripe refund state.

sara-finance: INV-2026-0421, CN-76841 (taxed), CN-76842 (untaxed). Stripe refund shows RN_3Kx... for CN-76841 only. Customer card shows charge still for $1,832.50. Screenshot: https://redwood.screens/abc123 (internal link)

mike-support: Ugh, we've seen PO+tax-exempt + legacy-tax-route create duplicate credits before. Possible race between proration job and PO validation. Repro steps?

sara-finance: Steps I used:
1) Create subscription with PO number and tax_exempt=true in account metadata.
2) Trigger downgrade via customer portal (calls PATCH /subscriptions/{id}).
3) Proration job runs and posts invoice via POST /invoices/create-proration -> creates two invoice items because tax engine path forks.
4) Billing orchestration issues two credit notes. Only one refund job enqueued because refund worker filters by invoice_id and CN-76842 references a legacy invoice token.

devon-eng: Can you share the exact API payloads (sanitized) you used? especially the proration job payload and any headers that indicate legacy_tax=true.

sara-finance: payloads pasted below (sanitized)
```
POST /invoices/create-proration
{
  "subscription_id": "sub_ABC",
  "change_type": "downgrade",
  "effective_at": "2026-03-09T12:34:00Z",
  "account": { "po_number": "PO-55678", "tax_exempt": true }
}
```
And the refund enqueue call: `POST /billing/refunds/enqueue` body contained `invoice_id: INV-2026-0421` which matched CN-76841 only.

devon-eng: OK this suggests two issues: 1) proration job created split credit notes because tax path forked; 2) refund worker selects by invoice->credit_note mapping that only links one CN. I'll add a quick guard to aggregate all CNs for the invoice before enqueueing refunds.

alex-billing: For remediation — we should issue an immediate manual refund for CN-76842 to the customer's card and create an adjusting journal to clear the partial balance. I'll do the manual Stripe refund but need approval for customer-visible note. @jules-cs can you confirm messaging?

jules-cs: Yep, we'll tell them: "We processed the missing partial refund and you'll see a separate credit on your card within 3-5 business days. We're also updating our billing logic to prevent duplicate credit notes for PO+tax-exempt flows." :white_check_mark:

billing-bot: Generated credit note CN-76843 to balance rounding delta (internal audit ref: AUD-1934).

mike-support: Also log this under ops-billing and tag engineers for follow-up. Suggest a small migration: when tax_exempt flag present, route proration through unified tax pipeline (no fork) or atomically create single credit note with tax lines attached.

devon-eng: I'll open a PR that changes the refund enqueue to `invoice_id -> lookup all credit_notes` and adds an integration test for PO+tax_exempt. Quick patch ETA end of day.

sara-finance: Appreciate it. For now I've filed a manual refund RN_3Kx... and emailed customer with the cs note. Leaving the thread for audit purposes. :lock:
